description: REQ-012's rewrite closes the FIND-001/FIND-002 (iteration-2) gap for REQ-001/REQ-002/REQ-006/REQ-011 (the Skip amount_in / BaseSigner tx-amount / computeSwapNeed-current choke points are now unambiguously integer bigint via toBaseUnits/fromBaseUnits, with exact-equality PROP-019/022/023 fixtures that a 10^6x-wrong decimals implementation genuinely fails). However, REQ-003 (source-funding precondition) was NOT routed through REQ-012 and now contains a self-contradictory unit identity for its threshold comparand, reintroducing the same class of unit-mismatch defect at a third call site REQ-012 claims to have eliminated ('THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT define, inline, or tolerate any second/alternate conversion between these unit spaces anywhere else in the codebase', behavioral-spec.md:431-432). REQ-003's EARS clause (behavioral-spec.md:179-181) names the comparand 'amountInRequiredByRoute' -- language that implies it is the already-integer, already-base-unit amount_in value produced by REQ-002's toBaseUnits() call (consistent with baseUsdcBalance, which is bigint per ChainReader.getBaseUsdc(): Promise<bigint>, verification-architecture.md:30). But REQ-003's own Acceptance Criteria two paragraphs later (behavioral-spec.md:194) renames the identical comparand 'neededUsd' -- language that implies a raw USD dollar float, exactly mirroring the parameter name used in checkSourceFunded's pure-function signature in verification-architecture.md:13 ('checkSourceFunded(baseUsdcBalance, baseGasBalance, neededUsd, minGasWei): boolean'). No REQ, pure function, or PROP anywhere defines what 'neededUsd' actually contains, whether it requires a toBaseUnits/fromBaseUnits conversion before being compared against the bigint baseUsdcBalance, or how 'amountInRequiredByRoute' (EARS) and 'neededUsd' (Acceptance Criteria + pure-fn signature) relate to each other -- REQ-003 uses two different names for what is presumably the same value without ever reconciling them. A spec-compliant implementer following the literal parameter name 'neededUsd' would naturally wire in the raw dollar float (e.g. capUsd(usdEquivalentOf(need, aktUsdPrice))'s output, ~15.32) and compare it directly against baseUsdcBalance (a bigint in base units, e.g. 20000000n for 20 USDC). Because on-chain base-unit balances are routinely 10^6x numerically larger than their dollar-float equivalent for any realistic wallet balance, a naive `baseUsdcBalance < neededUsd` comparison (bigint < number) would almost always evaluate false -- i.e. checkSourceFunded would report 'funded' even when the wallet holds only a tiny fraction of a cent of real USDC, directly violating REQ-003's explicit fail-closed / exact-deficit-reporting guarantee ('fail closed with the exact deficit... have X, need Y') and letting the driver proceed past the one precondition gate that exists specifically to catch today's real $0-balance blocker (REQ-003's own stated purpose, confirmed 'the live current blocker').

evidence.snippet: EARS (line 180): '...is `>= amountInRequiredByRoute` AND...' vs Acceptance Criteria (line 194): '`checkSourceFunded` returns `false` for every fixture where `baseUsdcBalance < neededUsd`...' -- two different names/units for the same comparand, neither routed through REQ-012's toBaseUnits/fromBaseUnits choke point, matching verification-architecture.md:13's `checkSourceFunded(baseUsdcBalance, baseGasBalance, neededUsd, minGasWei)` signature.

fix: Pick ONE name and ONE unit for checkSourceFunded's threshold parameter and use it consistently across REQ-003's EARS clause, its Acceptance Criteria, and verification-architecture.md's pure-function signature and PROP-005/PROP-006 descriptions. Given baseUsdcBalance is bigint base units, the comparand should be `amountInRequiredByRoute: bigint` -- explicitly defined as the exact same `toBaseUnits(capUsd(usdEquivalentOf(need, aktUsdPrice)), USDC_DECIMALS_BASE)` bigint value REQ-002/REQ-006 use (or the route-confirmed echo of it), never a re-derived or independently-named 'neededUsd' float. Rename the pure-function parameter accordingly and add an explicit REQ-012 clause routing REQ-003 through the same single choke point as REQ-001/002/006/011.
